\subsection*{Space Complexity --- Hierarchy: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Universal Simulation with a Space Bound]
\lean{Complexity.space_universal}
\label{Complexity.space_universal}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.TimeHierarchy.code, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.pairEncode}
There exists a finite-state binary Turing machine $S$ such that for every binary word
$\alpha$ there is a positive integer $C$ with the following property: for every
$s,t\in\mathbb{N}$ and binary words $x,y$, if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts on
input $x$ after exactly $t$ steps with output $y$ and uses at most $s$ work-tape cells
by that time, then $S$ halts on input $\langle
\mathrm{bin}(s),\langle\alpha,x\rangle\rangle$ with output $y$ at some time and uses at
most $Cs$ work-tape cells by then. Here $\mathrm{bin}(s)$ is the little-endian binary
representation of $s$, and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the specified self-delimiting
pairing of binary words.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Space hierarchy theorem]
\lean{Complexity.space_hierarchy}
\label{Complexity.space_hierarchy}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SpaceConstructible}
Let $f,g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be space-constructible functions. Suppose that for
every $A\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an $N$ such that $A f(n)\le g(n)$ for every $n\ge N$.
Then $\mathrm{SPACE}(f)$ is a proper subset of $\mathrm{SPACE}(g)$, where each class
consists of languages decidable by a finite binary Turing machine using at most a
constant multiple of the indicated space bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict inclusion of log space in polynomial space]
\lean{Complexity.LOGSPACE_ssubset_PSPACE}
\label{Complexity.LOGSPACE_ssubset_PSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.PSPACE}
The class of languages decidable by finite Turing machines using space bounded by a
constant multiple of $\log_2(n)+1$ is a proper subset of the class of languages
decidable using space bounded by a constant multiple of $n^c+1$ for some natural number
$c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear space differs from NP]
\lean{Complexity.SPACE_linear_ne_NP}
\label{Complexity.SPACE_linear_ne_NP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.SPACE}
The class of binary languages decidable by finite Turing machines using space bounded by
a constant multiple of the input length plus one is not equal to the class of languages
having polynomially bounded witnesses verifiable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}
